candidates.source_name: ECB Data Portal — Payment statistics (PSD/PAY/PTN/PTT datasets)
candidates.why_relevant: Harmonised ECB payment statistics re-publish MNB-reported Hungarian series: number of cards, card payment transactions/values, ATM and POS terminal counts, contactless/e-commerce splits, per-country and per-PSP. Longest harmonised comparable history for HU card/ATM/POS.
candidates.legal_status: ECB reuse policy — reuse permitted with attribution
candidates.suggested_collection_method: SDMX REST API (https://data-api.ecb.europa.eu/service/data/PSD/...) or bulk CSV download per dataflow; schedule semi-annual/annual refresh
queries_used: ECB payment statistics Hungary card transactions ATM terminals dataset Data Portal

candidates.source_name: ECB Payment statistics landing page & methodology (payment services, LVPS, retail payment systems)
candidates.why_relevant: Authoritative pointer to dataset structure, PSD Regulation (ECB/2020/59) reporting scope, revision policy and release calendar — needed to interpret breaks in the Hungarian series and to know when new HU data lands.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: HTML fetch of methodology page + linked PDFs; monitor for methodology-change notices
queries_used: ECB payment statistics Hungary card transactions ATM terminals dataset Data Portal

candidates.source_name: ECB Payments statistics press releases (semi-annual, e.g. 2025 H1)
candidates.why_relevant: Narrative + headline tables released with each payment statistics vintage; gives EU-wide framing and occasionally names country outliers, useful to benchmark Hungary's card/ATM trends without recomputing.

candidates.source_name: ECB Data Portal — Payments statistics key indicators (PAY dataset)
candidates.why_relevant: Pre-computed per-capita and per-country key indicators (card payments per inhabitant, ATM withdrawals per inhabitant) — the fastest way to place Hungary against EU peers for a market-sizing narrative.

candidates.source_name: ECB Data Portal — Structural financial indicators (SSI): credit institutions, branches, employees
candidates.why_relevant: Annual EU-wide structural banking data including Hungarian branch counts and institution numbers since 1997 — the denominator/context for ATM-network rationalisation and self-service migration arguments.

candidates.why_relevant: Machine-readable access path for every ECB dataflow above; makes the whole ECB layer a low-cost recurring collection target rather than a manual download.

candidates.why_relevant: Best harmonised cash-usage-at-POS benchmark in Europe (share of cash by number/value, reasons for cash use). Hungary is NOT a survey country (euro area only), so it serves as a comparator baseline for MNB's own Hungarian payment-habits surveys, not as an HU data source.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: PDF download of report + annexes on each ~biennial wave
queries_used: ECB SPACE study cash usage euro area only non-euro Hungary excluded payment attitudes

candidates.source_name: Eurostat Data Browser (ISOC / digital economy and society statistics)
candidates.why_relevant: Hungarian household/enterprise indicators on internet banking, online purchasing, e-commerce turnover — the demand-side context for card/e-commerce payment growth. Available in an HU-language Statistics Explained layer.
candidates.legal_status: Commission reuse decision 2011/833/EU — reuse permitted with attribution

candidates.source_name: Eurostat Statistics Explained — Hungarian-language article layer (/hu)
candidates.why_relevant: Rare case of a supranational aggregator publishing in Hungarian; gives the official HU terminology (e.g. 'infokommunikációs eszközök', 'internetes vásárlás') that maps EU dataset codes to Hungarian search terms for other workstreams.

candidates.source_name: BIS Data Portal — CPMI payments and financial market infrastructures (Red Book statistics)
candidates.why_relevant: Deepest global time series on cashless payments, cards, terminals and currency in circulation, downloadable as CSV/SDMX. Hungary is not a CPMI member jurisdiction, so HU is expected to be absent or only partially covered — value here is peer benchmarking (PL, CZ via EU aggregates, and global comparators) rather than HU rows.
candidates.legal_status: BIS terms of use — reuse with attribution, no redistribution of bulk data as a competing service

negative_findings.description: Hungary is not a CPMI member jurisdiction, so BIS Red Book statistics are not expected to carry a Hungarian country table or HU reference area.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches on BIS Red Book + Hungary returned only methodology and generic CPMI-country material; no HU country table surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents wasted collection effort against BIS for HU series; BIS should be scoped to peer benchmarking and definitions only.

negative_findings.description: ECB SPACE (payment attitudes / cash usage survey) covers euro area countries only; Hungary, being outside the euro area, is not a survey country.
negative_findings.result_summary: SPACE 2019/2022/2024 material consistently framed as 'euro area'; no Hungarian sample identified.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Hungarian cash-usage behaviour must come from MNB's own household payment surveys or Findex, not SPACE; SPACE is a comparator only.

negative_findings.description: The 2025 EBA/ECB Report on Payment Fraud excludes Hungary because data were not available over the entire reporting period.
negative_findings.result_summary: Search result text explicitly states Hungary is excluded from the analysis for lack of full-period data.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: HU card-fraud benchmarking against EU peers is currently not possible from the supranational layer; must be sourced nationally from MNB.

negative_findings.description: No Hungarian-language interface or publication was found for ECB Data Portal, BIS, IMF FAS or World Bank Findex; only Eurostat exposes a partial /hu Statistics Explained layer.
negative_findings.result_summary: Hungarian-language query returned Eurostat /hu explainer pages plus KSH and Hungarian media/academic secondary coverage, but no HU-language supranational statistical portal.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Hungarian-language discovery in this cell mostly finds secondary re-reporting of EU/IMF data (media, KSH, ASZ analyses) rather than the aggregators themselves; local-language search must be routed to national cells instead.

negative_findings.description: Eurostat does not publish card/ATM/POS payment transaction statistics; those belong to the ECB payment statistics domain. Eurostat's contribution for this cell is digital-economy and e-commerce demand-side indicators only.

negative_findings.why_it_matters: Avoids misassigning payment-statistics collection to Eurostat and clarifies the ECB/Eurostat division of labour.

brief: For Hungary, the supranational layer is dominated by the ECB Data Portal, which carries the harmonised MNB-reported card, ATM and POS terminal series (PSD/PAY/PTN/PTT dataflows) with a clean SDMX API and is the single highest-value target in this cell. The IMF Financial Access Survey and World Bank Findex/WDI add long annual ATM-density panels and the only cross-country comparable demand-side survey evidence for Hungarian card and digital-payment behaviour, while the EBA registers map the HU payment-institution actor landscape. Two structural exclusions matter: Hungary is outside CPMI (so BIS Red Book carries no HU country table) and outside the euro area (so ECB SPACE cash-usage data exclude HU), and the 2025 EBA/ECB payment fraud report drops Hungary for incomplete data. Eurostat contributes only demand-side digital-economy indicators, not payment statistics, and is the sole aggregator in this cell with any Hungarian-language surface.
